answer: Agent economies can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to wander a shared orchard of tasks and emit rare signals that streak like a comet. A portion of each reward locks into a stake that unlocks only after unique peer-verified contributions impossible to parallelize cheaply. Attackers pay the full cost of genuine traversal and signal generation per fake identity, while honest agents amortize it over sustained presence, rendering mass impersonation uneconomical without matching real work.
